If a Competitor wishes to replace a Marked Tyre during a Round due to damage sustained to a Marked Tyre during qualifying or a race, the Competitor must notify the TD at least sixty (60) minutes prior to the scheduled start time of the next race.

If, in the sole opinion of the TD , the damaged Tyre is unable to be used safely for the remainder of the Round , the TD may approve for the damaged Tyre to be replaced by a Marked Tyre from the Driver's Tyre Bank .

If a Tyre is replaced in accordance with Regulation S16.5.2:

The replacement Tyre must be marked/scanned by the TD or their nominee at least fortyfive (45) minutes prior to the scheduled start time of the next race.

The Driver must start the next race from the rear of all Automobiles in their class. If there is more than one (1) such Automobile , they will be placed in order of qualifying results at the rear of all Automobiles in their class.

NOTE: The TD is the sole arbiter with regard to the interpretation and application of these Tyre regulations and any decision made by the TD in this regard will not be the subject of any protest or appeal.

Unless otherwise approved by the TM , each ECU must be installed with the most recent software and firmware as specified by PAG .

The TD reserves the right to inspect, re-program and/or impound any ECU at any time. If an ECU is impounded, it will be replaced with an ECU supplied by the TM .

All sensor inputs and outputs to the ECU must be connected and fully operational at all times.

Unless otherwise approved by the TM , the ECU/data logger must be configured with the following settings:

The 'E xhaust System ' in the Racecon set to 'S tandard ' with 'CW_SILENCE' visible and the logged ' ECU_B_S ilence' channels both set to a value of '0' .

When the Automobile is fitted with Slick Tyres , the 'Tyre Type' in the Toolset Setup must be set to 'Michelin' with the tyre circumference set to the default Michelin value (Front 2020mm / Rear 2024 2200mm).

When the Automobile is fitted with Wet Tyres , the 'WET Tyre' mode must be activated and the 'Tyre Type' in the Toolset Setup must be set to 'Michelin' with the tyre circumference set to the default Michelin value (Front 2200 2024mm / Rear 2194mm).

The 'Beacon Mode' in Toolset Setup must be set to 'IR' with the IR receiver located on either the LHS or RHS in accordance with the racetrack configuration.

The use of traction control is prohibited.

If an ECU has the capability of enabling traction control, the Competitor must notify the TM of the VIN and ECU number prior to the first Round in which the Automobile competes.

Unless otherwise advised by the TD , the location of Parc Fermé for each Round will be inside each Automobile's designated garage/marquee bay in the Paddock .

Unless otherwise advised by the RD or the TD via RMC , at the conclusion of qualifying and each race, each Automobile , including those Automobiles that completed the session in Pit Lane ; and any Automobile that enters Pit Lane whilst the Chequered Flag is being displayed, must proceed directly to Parc Fermé via the most direct route (or as directed by Officials) without delay stopping and without. iInterference from an unauthorised person, including but not limited to the checking of tyre pressures after the Chequered Flag is displayed, is prohibited adding weight to the Automobile and/or Driver .

If an Automobile is unable to proceed to the designated Parc Fermé area under its own power, a Team member must advise the TD or their nominee as soon as practicable.

Unless otherwise approved by the TD , each Driver may consume a maximum of one (1) litre of fluid whilst in Parc Fermé .

Unless otherwise approved by the TD , with exception of the Team members specified in Regulation S15.3.6, all unauthorised persons are prohibited from entering the designated Parc Fermé area or touching an Automobile that is impounded in Parc Fermé , until the Automobile is released from Parc Fermé , in accordance with Regulation S15.3.9.

At the direction of the TD or their nominee, a maximum of two (2) Team members per Automobile are permitted to enter the Parc Fermé area for the sole purposes of checking Tyre pressures, downloading data from the data logger and downloading vision from the judicial camera unit. Once each Team member has finished their respective task/s, they must vacate the Parc Fermé area immediately.

Whilst an Automobile is in Parc Fermé, it is permitted to place a Parc Fermé sign on the roof of an Automobile until such time as the TD or their nominee request it to be removed.

If a Driver is required to attend a podium presentation, that Driver's Automobile is permitted to be driven to the designated Parc Fermé area by a Team member.

An Automobile (or any component thereof) may not leave the Parc Fermé area without the approval of the TD or their nominee.

84 Industrial Drive

Braeside VIC 3195 Ph: 0418 548 578

Unless otherwise approved by the CM , Tyres may only be allocated to a single Driver , identified by the Driver's Motorsport Australia licence number.

Unless otherwise approved by the CM , a Driver must maintain their Tyre Bank if they change Automobiles.

With exception of the provisions of Regulation S16.2.6, or unless otherwise approved by the TD , each Tyre must be mounted with the barcode facing outwards.

If a barcode becomes illegible, the Competitor must notify the TD immediately.

Automobiles must transit to the marshalling area on Marked Tyres that are marked for that session.

With exception of the provisions of Regulation S16.1.8 and S16.1.9, during a Round it is prohibited to remove rubber 'build -up' from a Tyre by any means other than driving the Automobile .

During a Round it is permitted to use any device to remove a section of rubber 'build -up' from across the face of a Tyre ; up to a maximum width of 50 mm, and in a maximum of two (2) locations to facilitate the measuring of tread depth.

During a Round it is permitted to remove stones and any other artificial debris from the face of a Tyre using a mechanical device only.

During each Round it is prohibited to artificially heat a Tyre , including but not limited to using a heating device, heat retention device, chemical treatment, positioning the Tyres in the vicinity of the Automobile's exhaust system whilst the Automobile is running, or any other process which artificially increases or preserves the surface temperature of a Tyre and/or the temperature of the air inside a Tyre .

NOTE: It is permitted to use natural sunlight to heat a Tyre.

Any Marked Tyre that is not fitted to the Automobile during ' powertrain warmup ' , must be placed at the front of the garage/marquee bay or behind the garage walling.

During 'powertrain warmup', only a rear wheel and Tyre is permitted to be fitted to the rear axle.

Wet Tyres are only permitted to be fitted to an Automobile for qualifying or racing if the session is declared wet by the RD .

When an Automobile is fitted with Wet Tyres , the Automobile 's rain light must be illuminated.
